title: Fix the Age Difference Calculator
description: The program should read two ages and print the numeric difference between them. Fix the bug.
buggyCode:
age1 = input("Enter first age: ")
age2 = input("Enter second age: ")
print(age1 - age2)
expectedBehavior: The program should subtract the second age from the first and print the numeric result.
actualProblem: input() always returns a string, and Python does not support the - operator between two strings, so a TypeError is raised.
correctedCode:
age1 = int(input("Enter first age: "))
age2 = int(input("Enter second age: "))
print(age1 - age2)
expectedOutput: Enter first age: Enter second age: 5
explanation: Values from input() must be explicitly converted with int() (or float()) before they can be used in arithmetic. Without the conversion, Python treats them as text and refuses the subtraction.
